Prevention: Anthracnose is a fungal disease that reproduces by spores spread by wind, water, infested plants and tools.
Remove all crop residues for previous crops and neighbouring farms from tomato, egg plants, potato and peppers.
But do not remove debris and residues if no major pest problem is in the field, to improve soil.
Only plant seedlings that are disease free.
Avoid excess of too much water in the field for reducing transmission of disease.
Select well the site on well drained land.
Stake the tomatoes and do a bit pruning of plants to keep them high and dry with plenty of air.
Mulch tomatoes to prevent the fruits from coming into contact with soil.
Weed regularly and avoid overhead irrigation to reduce period of wetness on tomato fruit.
Harvest fruits promptly since anthracnose develops more readily as the fruit ages and to reduce spread of the disease.
Crop rotation (with three years breaks) because anthracnose can be a soil borne diseases.
Rotate with for example maize, cassava.
Monitoring: Anthracnose at seedling stage, vegetative stage and fruiting stage.
Increase inspection during wet season to twice a week.
Look on the leaves, on the stem and on the fruits.
Foliar symptoms are circular brown lesion surrounding by yellow halo.
Some roots can be split to search for brown and decayed internal tissue with many small black dots below the surface of the roots.
Water soaked circular spots on the fruit.
To act if 2-4 plants over 10 sampled plants are affected (if the leaves show circular brown lesion surrounding by yellow halo).
The action is too late when plant complete fruiting.
Direct Control: Remove all plants affected and burn.
Usually at 2ml x 20l of water, but double check label.
Restrictions: The farmers can be updated on the list of pesticides at
RAB stations at least every year.
Follow the instruction on the product label.
Infected plants cannot be cured by fungicides.
Foliar sprays of protective fungicides may help a bit to prevent infection of healthy plants.
L of water, but double check label.
Spray earlier morning or late of the day.
Toxicity to earthworms and fish: avoid spraying near water bodies.
